text.title: Retro Format Rotation Guide: Failure Modes
text.summary: 6 known failure modes when rotating retro formats across cycles for the same team. Each carries a detector (what to look for) and a repair (the corrective action).

failure-mode.description: Three sailboats: the team has run the same format three times running because "everyone likes it"; the third column is empty and action items have dried up.
failure-mode.detector: `next_format` present in `last_3_formats`; a format appearing twice or more in the last three; action-item count falling across those instances.
failure-mode.repair: Pick a format outside the last three and name the previous three in the rationale (`r-no-repeat-in-last-3`, `r-rationale-names-history-state-and-tiebreaker`).

failure-mode.description: History from memory: `last_3_formats` was typed from recollection, the actual instances say otherwise, and the "fresh" pick is a repeat.
failure-mode.detector: `last_3_formats` does not match the formats recorded in the three most recent committed retro instances; fewer than three committed instances exist but a `next_format` was emitted.
failure-mode.repair: Rebuild the history from the committed instances, newest first; with fewer than three, record `skip: history < 3` and do not pick (`r-history-read-from-committed-instances`).

failure-mode.description: Live format for an async team: rotation "for variety" lands an async team on lean-coffee or mad-sad-glad; the overlap-hour timezone gets a retro and the rest get a summary.
failure-mode.detector: `team_state.distribution == async` with `next_format` in {mad-sad-glad, lean-coffee}, or any format scheduled without anonymous asynchronous input and a timezone-spanning window.
failure-mode.repair: Rotate within the async-capable pool with anonymous input on a shared board; record the exception when the pool is exhausted (`r-async-team-rotates-within-async-pool`).

failure-mode.description: Blind stale detector: no action-item or participant counts were recorded for the last two scheduled retros, so the detector cannot fire and the rotation is a random walk.
failure-mode.detector: Outcome review entries for the last two scheduled retros lack action-item count, participant count or silent-participant count.
failure-mode.repair: Backfill the counts from the retro instances before emitting the next pick; block the pick until they exist (`r-counts-recorded-per-scheduled-retro`).

failure-mode.description: Fatigued team gets the fourth-most-recent format: the no-repeat rule is satisfied, but the team ran that format two quarters ago and has full muscle memory for it; nothing refreshes.
failure-mode.detector: `fatigue_signal == fatigued` and `next_format` was used by this team within the last 12 months; rationale does not state when the format was last used.
failure-mode.repair: Pick a format unused for 12 months or never used, and state the last-used date in the rationale (`r-fatigued-team-picks-format-unused-12-months`).

failure-mode.description: Morale treated as a format problem: five formats in five cycles, participation still falling, and the guide keeps picking a sixth instead of naming the real variable.
failure-mode.detector: Two consecutive rotations to non-stale formats with no increase in action-item or contributing-participant counts; rotation continues without a team-health review recorded.
failure-mode.repair: Record `fatigue is not a format problem`, suspend rotation, and route to the morale pulse or burnout-tripwire methodology (`r-two-rotations-without-refresh-escalate-to-team-health`, `r-stale-format-detector-three-signals`).
